items.prompt: How does LexicalRetriever tokenize the strings billing-api and BillingService?
items.answer: billing-api becomes two tokens; BillingService becomes billingservice
distractors: Both are split in two, once at the dash and once at the capital B
billing-api stays one token; BillingService becomes billing, service
Both stay single tokens, since dashes and capitals are both kept
items.explanation: Tokens are runs of [a-z0-9]+ matched after ToLowerInvariant. The dash is not in the class, so billing-api splits into billing and api. Lowercasing happens before matching, so the capital S is no boundary and BillingService is one token.

items.prompt: LexicalRetriever.Search is called with the query "investigate the service incident". What does it return?
items.answer: Nothing, because every word in that query is a stop word
distractors: The top three documents by title, since all of them score 0
Documents tagged incident, as stop words apply to content only
An ArgumentException, since the term list must not be empty
items.explanation: The stop-word set includes the domain words incident, investigate and service as well as the. After filtering there are no query terms, and line 24 returns an empty array. Stop words are removed from the query only, and nothing throws.

items.prompt: A runbook's content contains the word queue ten times and nowhere else. The query is just queue. What happens to that runbook?
items.answer: It scores 1 and is dropped by the default minimum score of 3
distractors: It scores 10, since each occurrence in the content counts once
It scores 1 and is still returned as the only matching runbook
It scores 3, since repeated content matches are capped at three
items.explanation: Each field is turned into a set, so ten occurrences count once, and content is worth 1. The default minimumScore is 3, and the Where on line 27 removes matches below it.

items.prompt: The service test scores its runbook against the incident's retrieval query. What heuristicScore does the runbook get?
distractors: 24: timeout adds 7 more from its title and tags
16: payment and payments merge into a single term
12: only the title and tag matches are counted
items.explanation: billing is in title, tags and content (4+3+1), capture in title and content (4+1), payments in tags (3), payment in content (1): 17. The incident says time out (two tokens), so timeout never matches, and there is no stemming to merge payment and payments. Content matches count 1 each.

items.prompt: Two documents both score 6. One is titled "apple runbook", the other "Billing runbook". Which comes first?
items.answer: apple runbook, as ties are broken by title ignoring case
distractors: Billing runbook, since uppercase sorts before lowercase
Whichever one was stored first, as ties keep input order
Whichever has the smaller DocumentId, which is compared first
items.explanation: After OrderByDescending(score), ThenBy uses StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase on the title, so apple sorts before Billing. A case-sensitive ordinal sort would put B (66) before a (97), but that is not the comparer used. DocumentId is only the final tie-breaker.

items.prompt: Search is called with topK: 0. What comes back?
items.answer: An empty list; a nonpositive bound means nothing
distractors: Every passing document, as 0 means no limit at all
An ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the first guard
The single best match, since topK is raised to 1
items.explanation: Line 22 returns [] when topK <= 0 or minimumScore <= 0. The guide stresses that nonpositive bounds mean nothing, not unbounded. There is no exception and no clamping.

items.prompt: A user with the Viewer role calls POST /api/incidents/{id}/run-investigation. Where is the request stopped?
items.answer: At the CanInvestigate policy, with a 403 before any service code
distractors: In OperationsService, whose exception the middleware maps to 401
Nowhere; Viewers may run investigations but cannot approve them
In the controller, which returns a 404 to hide that the incident exists
items.explanation: The action carries [Authorize(Policy = "CanInvestigate")], and that policy requires the Admin or Engineer role, so authorization fails with 403 before the action runs. The service check is a second line of defense, and its exception maps to 403, not 401.

items.prompt: RequestContext.FromClaims is given a principal with a name identifier but no role claim. Which Role does the context get?
items.answer: Viewer, so a missing role defaults to the least privilege
distractors: Engineer, the default role given to authenticated users
null, and IsAdminOrEngineer then throws a NullReferenceException
Admin, because the role check is skipped when no claim exists
items.explanation: Line 11: FindFirst(ClaimTypes.Role)?.Value ?? "Viewer". The guide notes this makes the default the least privilege. Role is never null, and nothing grants Engineer or Admin by default.

items.prompt: An Admin token passes the CanInvestigate policy but has no NameIdentifier claim. What status does run-investigation return?
distractors: 403, because a missing user id is treated as the Viewer role
500, because Guid.Parse is called on a null string value
401, because JwtBearer requires a name identifier claim
items.explanation: FromClaims uses ?? throw new InvalidOperationException(...) when the claim is missing, so Guid.Parse never runs. The middleware maps InvalidOperationException to 400 (BadRequest). The Viewer default applies to a missing role, not a missing id, and the token itself was valid.

items.prompt: How many times does RunIncidentInvestigationAsync call SaveChangesAsync?
items.answer: Once, at the end, for run, tool calls, approval and audit row
distractors: Twice: once for the agent run, then once for the approval
Once per entity it adds, which is six calls in total
Never; the outbox worker saves those rows a little later
items.explanation: The method adds the AgentRun, two AgentToolCalls, the HumanApproval and an AuditEvent, changes the tracked incident, and then calls SaveChangesAsync once on line 434. The outbox worker plays no part in this path.

items.prompt: An investigation has created a HumanApproval with Status Pending. How can an Admin approve it through the API?
items.answer: They cannot: the approvals controller only lists the rows
distractors: POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve, which is open to Admins
By a PATCH to the incident, which approves its latest run
The outbox worker approves it once all evidence is saved
items.explanation: ApprovalsController has a single [HttpGet] List action. No endpoint decides an approval, and the row has no foreign key to the run or incident; the guide calls Pending the end of the line. The outbox worker does not touch approvals.

items.prompt: Which log rows does the investigation count as evidence?
items.answer: The primary service's rows from DetectedAt minus 2 hours up to now
distractors: The newest 20 rows of any service, sorted by their timestamp
Rows within one hour either side of the incident's DetectedAt
Rows from every service listed in AffectedServicesCsv
items.explanation: logWindowStart = incident.DetectedAt.AddHours(-2), logWindowEnd = startedAt, and the predicate filters ServiceName == incident.PrimaryService. Twenty is the sample size of the id list, not the evidence filter, and the affected services CSV goes into the retrieval query only.

items.prompt: 500 log rows match the investigation's predicate. What do evidenceCount and evidenceIds hold?
items.answer: 500, and the ids of the 20 newest of those rows
distractors: 20, and the ids of those same 20 rows
500, and the ids of the 20 oldest rows
500, and all 500 ids in timestamp order
items.explanation: One predicate, two queries: CountAsync gives the full 500; the id query orders by Timestamp descending (then Id), takes 20 and selects ids. Descending order means newest first, and Take(20) bounds the list.

items.front: LexicalRetriever scoring rules in one breath.
items.back: Tokens = [a-z0-9]+ after lowercasing; 14 stop words removed from the query only; query terms distinct; each field a set; weights title 4, tags 3, content 1 (additive); keep score >= 3; order score desc, title ignore-case, id; Take(topK); nonpositive topK or minimumScore -> empty.

1) route + CanInvestigate policy; 2) claims -> RequestContext; 3) service role check again; 4) tracked incident load (404 if missing); 5) log evidence (count + 20 ids); 6) load all knowledge documents and rank in memory; 7) AgentRun, 2 tool calls, HumanApproval, incident update, audit event, one SaveChangesAsync.

items.front: What the investigation path does NOT do.
items.back: No model call (modelUsed false, modelConfidence null); no approval decision (only a GET list, and HumanApproval has no FK to the run or incident); no mitigation executes. Pending is the end of the line.
